cost: WEMBANYAMA'S RIMPROT 99 IS DECLINED, and the price is measured rather than argued. He reads 97 and his '24 and '25 cards read 97 too, both anchored (recal_82 at 97 tol 0, recal_53 at 97 tol 1), so the 20/60/20 smoothing means '26 cannot move without them. THREE ceilings hold him, and only all three together reach 99: (1) ID is clamped to 1.0 before Prot ranks it, and his composite is 1.2446 - the same clamp recal_97 removed from perdef, never removed here; (2) the tracked rim term is a within-season PERCENTILE, so his -8.6% reads 0.959 rather than 1.0 because he is 2026's 4.5th percentile and not its single best; (3) that term is applied to EVERY card including a unanimous DPOY, where perdef routes a voted card past it. Measured: unclamping alone gives 98 and costs 4 tol-0 anchors (Gobert '19 and Wembanyama '24 97 -> 98, Mutombo '97 and Duncan '03 98 -> 99). Routing votes past the tracked percentile alone gives 98 and costs Wembanyama '24 (97 -> 96, DOWN). Both together give 99 and cost 5 anchors AND take the pool from 9 cards at 99 to 48 - eight Gobert seasons and seven Duncan seasons all reading exactly 99, which is the compression recal_84 and recal_90 exist to prevent. Tightening the band slope to 0.45 to thin that crowd pushes Ben Wallace '04 98 -> 96 and Bobby Jones '82 96 -> 94, i.e. it pays for the summit by deflating the board. THE STRUCTURAL POINT: Wembanyama '24 has a BETTER rim sheet than '26 (blk 10.0% vs 9.4%, tracked rim -10.7% vs -8.6%, same height, same votes) and is anchored at 97 tol 0, so no monotone formula puts '26 at 99 and leaves '24 at 97. Tomer decides: either the '24 anchor is re-opened, or 97 stands.

THE FROZEN CONTROLS MOVED, and this is the round's real cost, stated first rather than buried. Stephen Curry '16 perdef 52 -> 69, Kevin Durant '25 42 -> 70, Deandre Ayton '20 41 -> 68, LaMarcus Aldridge '20 36 -> 63, Trae Young '22 40 -> 50. These are NOT a defect and they are NOT reachable by tuning around: Curry '16 defended 703 shots at -5.8% and Durant '25 543 at -5.2%, both fuller AND better readings than the ruling's own subject (Castle, -1.5% on 514, ruled to the low 60s), so under one formula they must read above him. Measured across the whole ceiling sweep: even LEAVING the blend ceiling at recal_12's 0.70, retiring the backwards targeting discount alone takes Curry to 62 and Durant to 59. The tuning knob does not separate them from Castle; only a per-player override would, and that is forbidden. RECORDED FOR TOMER: if the Durant/Curry class is wrong, the thing to re-open is Castle's number, not the discount.

recal_92 IS PARTLY CORRECTED BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, and the correction is in that round's own terms. recal_92 wrote "it does not improve with sample: at a 250-attempt floor it is 0.363" and set rho flat at 0.345. Measured over a wider range on the same file, reliability climbs to 0.406 at 350, 0.431 at 450, 0.502 at 550 and 0.528 at 650 — the 250-attempt step was simply too short to see the trend. The doctrine of recal_92 stands (a season's diff is an estimate and must be regressed); what changes is that the amount of regression now depends on how much evidence there is. Kevin Durant '25, whom recal_92's receipt named as the pathology of the r16 floor at 76, now reads 70 by a different mechanism: not an absolute floor that ignored sample and composite, but a 543-shot measurement regressed by its measured reliability.

notes: WHY CASTLE READ 50, term by term. Composite 0.497 (no votes, so it is shrunk toward 0.5 and carries almost nothing), tracked reading 60.8 in card space from -1.5% over 514 shots. The blend weight that decides between them was wm = 0.70 x targeting x sample = 0.70 x 0.35 x 1.00 = 0.245 — so 75% of his card was a number designed to be uninformative, and the 0.35 was a HUNTED discount applied because he defended 2.1x the season median. A full season of evidence bought him less weight than a 180-shot season would have.

THE TARGETING DISCOUNT'S PREMISE, tested and found backwards. It assumed high volume means a harder shot diet. Over all 6,875 tracked cards, corr(attempts / season median, diff) = -0.068, and every bucket runs the other way: <0.5x median +2.14% (sd 15.11%), 0.5-1.0x +1.61% (4.39%), 1.0-1.5x +1.07% (3.62%), 1.5-2.0x +0.83% (3.16%), 2.0-2.5x +0.64% (2.93%), >2.5x +0.16% (2.62%). Men who defend the most shots have BETTER diffs and LESS noise — the discount cut the truest and most reliable readings by up to 65%, and it fought _sample_weight, which rewards the same volume, card for card.

RELIABILITY RISES WITH THE SAMPLE, which is the half of recal_92 that was measured too narrowly. Outside 6Ft, year-over-year, both seasons above the floor: 150+ r=0.345 (n=3,181), 250+ 0.363 (2,350), 350+ 0.406 (1,540), 450+ 0.431 (813), 550+ 0.502 (314), 650+ 0.528 (95). Overall: 150+ 0.355, 350+ 0.421, 550+ 0.471, 750+ 0.577. The curve in the file IS this table, interpolated — nothing is fitted.

FULL_SAMPLE 350 -> 500. recal_12 set "full workload = full evidence" at 350 by assertion. The median tracked card in this file defends 452 shots from 6ft+ (p75 546, p90 631, p99 820), so 350 was the 35th percentile of workload and `samp` saturated for two thirds of the pool — which is why the targeting weight ended up doing all the discriminating. 500 sits just above the median. It is also what holds Ajay Mitchell '26: at 344 shots he is two thirds of a full sample where Castle is a full one, so he gains 3 points where Castle gains 10, and recal_92's band holds.

WHY WEMBANYAMA READ 58 WITH THE BEST TRACKED SHEET IN THE POOL. His voted-band weight is 1.00, and the line was PD2 = (1-wv)*tracked + wv*band — so his -8.6% over 765 shots was multiplied by ZERO. He was ranked purely on a composite that his height empties twice (0.463 of a possible 1.09), putting him at the 8th percentile of voted defenders. The fix does not touch the height terms he accepts: it stops the measurement being discarded. It is a floor and never a ceiling, so Kawhi '17, Dort '26, Herbert Jones '23, Dyson Daniels '25 and Amen Thompson '25 — voted men whose band already beats their tracked read — are all exactly flat.

FOOTPRINT: 2,580 perdef cards move, 2,429 up and 151 down, max 28, 1,493 by 5+. The asymmetry is structural and worth naming: recal_86 centred the absolute tracked line at 58 ("allowed exactly what was expected") while the no-vote composite band sits around 35-52, so ANY round that trusts tracking more pulls the no-vote population up toward 58 from below. That is why even Trae Young '22, whose diff is bad, rises. rimprot moves on ZERO cards and o_ovr on ZERO.

JAYLEN BROWN '26 IS THE ROUND'S OWN CONTROL, arrived at independently. He was not in the design set: his ruling came in during the integration, on a card with the same shape as the subject but a fuller sample and a better diff (587 shots at -3.6% against Castle's 514 at -1.5%). The formula puts him six points above Castle without being asked to, and Tomer accepted that number as-is. A ruling that lands on a card the round never targeted is the strongest evidence the shape is right.

THE ERA-RELATIVE INDEX PROVED ITSELF HERE. recal_100 subtracts each season's own defensive level before the gauge. This round raised perdef across the tracked era only (2014+), so the raw drtgRef of every modern five improved at once — exactly the kind of level shift that would have wrecked a fixed scale. Because the index is era-relative, re-deriving it moved the 2014+ levels down by ~0.6 and left 1980-2013 within 0.03, and every one of recal_100's rulings survived unchanged on the new block.
